第1194章 帮它记起来（第1页）
雾团蜷在卡拉斯掌心前半寸的位置，边缘还在极轻极轻极轻地散着。刚才碰茧印的那一丝雾丝已经缩回去了，但缩回去之后没有再蜷成之前那么紧的一团。
它在茧印的温度里极缓极慢极沉极重极古极老极韧极稳极静极柔极透极轻极未知地舒展了一丝。
只是舒展，不是散，和它刚感应到冰层存在推劲时那种散法不同——那时候散是太久没有碰过任何东西，连自己的边界都忘了。现在舒展是因为有人告诉它还在这里。
它说它叫雾。以前有过别的名字，等太久太久太久，都忘了，只剩下雾。它的声音不是从某个中心点发出的，是从雾团每一丝边缘同时极轻极轻极轻地渗出来的，每个字都裹着极浓极浓极浓的雾，飘到一半就开始散。
拼碎片的人听到这句话，光丝在它背后极轻极轻极轻地颤了一下。它说它以前也没有名字，它醒来的时候只是一堆碎片，每片之间没有任何连接，只是飘着。
它不知道自己叫什么，也不知道自己以前是不是有完整的形状，它只知道自己是一堆碎片。
后来它花了很久很久很久学会用碎片边缘磨丝，把自己绑在一起，才拼成现在这个人形。它说它不是碎片，它是拼碎片的人，它的名字是自己起的——它做的最久的一件事，就是它的名字。
卡拉斯把手掌翻过来，掌心朝下，茧印对着地面。冰层那个存在也不是一开始就会碰。
它在冰里裹了很久很久很久，卡拉斯第一次把手覆在掌印上时它连回应都不敢，只是极轻极轻极轻地敲了一下冰壁。后来它学会了敲，学会了推，学会了碰，学会了把冷拆成收放快慢碰推，学会了写曲子。
它现在在冰层深处侧着，每隔片刻极轻极轻极轻地敲一下冰壁，敲它刚写完的那首曲子。那个存在说曲子是它写的，它不是谁。
他告诉雾，它也一样——不用记得以前叫什么，它现在就是雾，雾就是名字。以后它学会了别的东西，再给自己起新的名字，和阿卡一样——阿卡刚来铁城时也没有名字，后来她自己起了。
雾团极轻极轻极轻地一震。这一下不是抖，不是缩，是它在试着把自己聚拢。它飘在这里太久太久太久，久到忘了怎么保持形状，那些边缘一直在散，散到虚空里就再也收不回来。
现在它试着把散的边缘收回来，但收不回来——那些散出去的雾丝飘得太远太远太远了，远到它自己都感应不到。它连自己的边界都找不回来，它从来不敢收，怕收的时候更散，连现在这一团都保不住。
卡拉斯把手掌重新翻过来，掌心朝上，茧印正对着雾团。他把暗爪翼尖茧火的暖、老穆拉丁锤柄铁纹里火星子的稳、烬藤攀过铆钉时藤尖的触感、阿卡端碗时碗底推手心的推劲、冰层存在碰冰壁的碰劲，全部从茧印里极轻极轻极轻地渗出来。
这些温度在他掌心上铺成极薄极薄极薄的一层膜，比雾团最边缘的雾丝还薄，但比雾丝更韧更稳更连贯。
他说这是茧，茧不是用来裹自己的，是用来收温度的，冷和暖都能收。他的茧能收住冰层的冷，也能收住铁城的暖。它不需要急着把散出去的雾丝全收回来——先用这片茧膜裹住现在还在的部分，把这一小团裹稳，以后再把散出去的慢慢找回来。
雾团极轻极轻极轻地往前探了一丝。这次探得比刚才更稳——不是碰，是学。它在学茧膜怎么裹东西。茧印上的温度极轻极轻极轻，它学着茧膜把自己边缘极轻极轻极轻地往里卷了一丝。
它散开的边缘在卷起来的瞬间裹住了茧印上渗出来的一点温度，卷和裹，这两个动作它以前不会，茧膜教它了。
它卷起边缘之后把自己裹住了——不是茧印帮它裹的，是它自己用卷起来的边缘把还在的核心裹住。
核心还是很小很小很小，边缘还是不断往外散，但散的边缘在茧膜的温度里开始极缓极慢极沉极重极古极老极韧极稳极静极柔极透极轻极未知地往回卷。
它自己学会了卷，学会了裹，下一步就可以学怎么把散出去的雾丝收回来。它不再只是一团等散的雾了。

Chapter 1194 Help it remember (page 1)
The mist curled up half an inch in front of Karas's palm, and the edges were still spreading very lightly. The trace of mist that touched the cocoon mark just now has retracted, but after retracting, it did not curl up into as tight a ball as before.
In the temperature of the cocoon mark, it is extremely slow, extremely slow, extremely heavy, extremely ancient, extremely old, extremely tough, extremely stable, extremely static, extremely soft, extremely transparent, extremely light, extremely light, extremely light, extremely light, extremely gentle, and stretches in an unknown way.
It's just stretching, not scattering, which is different from the way it dispersed when it first sensed the push from the ice - at that time it had not touched anything for so long that it had even forgotten its own boundaries. It stretches now because someone told it to still be here.
It says it's called fog. There were other names before, but after waiting for too long, too long, they were all forgotten, and only the fog remained. Its sound does not come from a certain central point, but oozes out from every edge of the fog at the same time. Every word is wrapped in extremely dense fog, which begins to disperse halfway through.
When the person who pieced the pieces together heard these words, the light thread trembled very lightly behind it. It said that it had no name before. When it woke up, it was just a pile of fragments. There was no connection between each piece, and it was just floating.
It doesn't know what its name is, and it doesn't know whether it had a complete shape before. It only knows that it is a pile of fragments.
Later, it took a long, long, long time to learn to grind the edges of the fragments and tie them together to form the human form it has now. It says that it is not a fragment, it is the person who put the fragments together, and that it gave its name to itself - the thing it has done for the longest time is its name.
Karas turned his hand over, palm down, with the cocoon mark facing the ground. The existence of the ice layer is not something you will touch at the beginning.
It had been wrapped in the ice for a long, long time. When Karas put his hand on the palm print for the first time, it didn't even dare to respond. It just tapped the ice wall very lightly. Later, it learned to knock, push, and bump, learn to divide the cold into fast and slow push, and learned to write music.
It is now lying on its side deep in the ice, tapping the ice wall very lightly every moment, tapping the song it just finished writing. That being said that the music was written by it and not by anyone else.
He told the fog that it was the same - no need to remember what it was called before, it was just the fog now, and the fog was the name. Later, it learned other things and gave itself a new name, just like Aka - Aka didn't have a name when she first came to Iron City, but she later picked it up on her own.
The mist shook very lightly. This time it's not shaking or shrinking, it's just trying to gather itself together. It has been floating here for so long, so long, that it has forgotten how to maintain its shape. The edges have been scattering, and they can never be recovered after being scattered into the void.
Now it tried to pull back the scattered edges, but it couldn't - the scattered mist drifted too far, too far, too far, so far that it couldn't sense it. It can't even find its own boundary. It never dares to close it, for fear that when it does, it will scatter even more, and it won't even be able to keep the current group.
Karas turned his palm over again, with his palm facing up, and the cocoon mark was facing the mist. He put the warmth of the cocoon fire on the wingtips of the dark claws, the stability of the sparks in the iron pattern of the handle of old Muradin's hammer, the touch of the tip of the vine when climbing over the rivet, the push of the bottom of the bowl against the palm of Aka's hand when he held the bowl, and the force of the ice layer hitting the ice wall, all of which seeped out from the cocoon mark very lightly.
These temperatures formed an extremely thin film on his palm, thinner than the mist threads at the edge of the fog mass, but tougher, more stable and more coherent than the fog threads.
He said that this is a cocoon. The cocoon is not used to wrap oneself, but to absorb temperature. It can absorb both cold and warmth. His cocoon can contain the coldness of the ice and the warmth of the iron city. It doesn't need to rush to take back all the scattered mist threads - first use this cocoon membrane to wrap the part that is still there, wrap this small ball firmly, and then slowly retrieve the scattered mist threads later.
The mist moved forward very lightly. This time the exploration was more stable than before - not touching, but learning. It is learning how to wrap things in its cocoon. The temperature on the cocoon print is very light, very light, very light, and it imitates the cocoon membrane and rolls its edges inward very lightly.
Its loose edges wrapped around a little bit of the warmth seeping out of the cocoon mark when it was rolled up. Rolling and wrapping were two actions it didn't know how to do before, and the cocoon membrane taught it.
It rolled up the edges and wrapped it around itself - it wasn't the cocoon mark that wrapped it up, it was itself using the rolled up edges to wrap up the core that was still there.
The core is still very small, very small, and the edges are still spreading out, but in the temperature of the cocoon membrane, the scattered edges begin to roll back very slowly, very slowly, very sinking, very heavy, very ancient, very old, very tough, very stable, very still, very soft, very transparent, very light, very unknown.
It has learned to roll and wrap it by itself, and the next step is to learn how to take back the dispersed mist threads. It's no longer just a fog waiting to clear.
